item.title: The EU’s Budget Talks Raise Serious Questions for the UN
item.description: The European Union is negotiating its next seven-year budget for the period from 2028 to 2034. So far, there has been limited dialogue between Europe’s budget negotiators and key United Nations agencies on this matter — as they are likely to be affected — but a recent letter from Secretary-General António Guterres to the EU ... item.title: Reforming the UN Must Begin with Reforming Staff Representation
item.description: Stronger staff representation means a stronger United Nations. This is not simply about protecting jobs or preserving acquired benefits, important as those objectives are. This is about protecting the institutional capacity, integrity and independence of the United Nations itself. item.title: COP31 opens in Antalya: Can climate promises finally deliver results?
item.description: Nearly 200 countries have arrived on Türkiye's Mediterranean coast for a climate summit with a different ambition: fewer grand declarations and more concrete decisions. With a powerful El Niño threatening to worsen extreme weather, negotiators face difficult questions over climate finance, clean energy and how to protect communities already living with the consequences of climate change.

item.title: Families who fled Ethiopia for Kenya’s Moyale need food, water and shelter
item.description: The International Organization of Migration (IOM) and partners are calling for urgent funding to support tens of thousands of people who have escaped violent clashes in Ethiopia for the Moyale region in northern Kenya.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Strikes on Ukraine’s power grid, as peace talks loom
item.description: The Security Council is meeting in New York on Ukraine. Russian strikes on energy infrastructure are threatening millions with another cold, dark winter, and civilian deaths are climbing sharply. The meeting comes on the eve of US-backed talks due to take place in Abu Dhabi. Follow our live meeting coverage below.

item.title: ‘Exceptional’ extreme temperatures to continue into next year, UN reports
item.description: In April this year, roughly 146.5 million Indians were exposed to an extreme heatwave with temperatures hitting a sweltering 47℃.

item.title: World News in Brief: El Niño’s $11 trillion price tag, Mozambique and Yemen updates
item.description: The El Niño extreme weather pattern could cost the global economy up to $11 trillion and seriously impact food security, said the UN agency tackling rural poverty in developing countries on Monday.

item.title: Children among the dead as heavy rains flood tents and shelters in Gaza
item.description: An infant reportedly drowned and five Gazans were killed – including three children – when a sand dune collapsed on their tents as the first heavy rains swept across the enclave at the weekend, according to the UN aid coordination office (OCHA).

item.title: Drought Cripples Dairy Farmers in Maharashtra in ‘Off the Charts’ Weather Year
item.description: For farmers in the Solapur district in the western Indian state of Maharashtra, extreme weather isn't a distant reality but a lived experience. They are the people Celeste Saulo, WMO Secretary General, refers to when she comments that 'behind the headlines and the statistics in this report are people who suffered the loss of loved ones, threats to their health and safety, flooded homes, failed harvests, empty shelves, lack of water and choking air.
